article:
A folder becomes a URL

Hosting is a computer that is always on, serving your files. Vercel is the one this house uses. You connect the GitHub repo. Every push can become a preview. One branch — usually main — is production. Production is the site people mean when they type the name.

Preview is the draft. Production is the promise. Mixing them up is how you demo the wrong thing.

What you actually click

Import the repo. Wait. Visit the .vercel.app URL. If the page is blank, the build failed — open the log, paste the red text back to Grok. If the page is old, you are looking at a cached tab or the wrong project.

Two projects on one domain is a classic mess. This site had an old well on the apex and the new paper on www. The lesson is rude and useful: check both, then pick one project to own the name.

How I actually do it

Push to main. Let Vercel rebuild. If the function needs a secret, it will not work until the env var is there and you redeploy. Adding GITHUB_TOKEN did nothing until production was rebuilt. The dashboard is part of the craft, not a side quest.

Where noobs get stuck

Downloading a zip and emailing it. Calling that shipped. Or connecting the wrong repo, or the right repo on the wrong team. Or waiting for “custom infrastructure.” You do not need a server you can SSH into. You need a URL that does not die when you close the lid.

Film this

The Vercel import screen. The first .vercel.app load. A push, a rebuild, a refresh. Then flip production versus preview and say the difference out loud.

Do this before chapter 07

  • Connect the repo from chapter 05.
  • Load the preview URL on your phone.
  • Change one line, push, confirm the preview moved.
  • Write down the production URL. That is the thing you will point a domain at.

Next: domains and DNS — buy a name, point it, survive the freeze.
